title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typescript page (numbered '- 22 -') is not part of the 1965 motives material on the facing pages. It is a draft in Bourbaki style on analytic functions over a complete valued field K, close in spirit to Bourbaki's 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques' and to Serre's 'Lie Algebras and Lie Groups', Part II. The internal cross-references 'Fonct.var.réelle, chap.I, §2' and 'Top.gén. chap.IV, §2' are Bourbaki references. The sheet was probably reused or misfiled in the dossier.

Corollary (local inverse function theorem). Let u: A ⊂ K^p → K^p be analytic and a ∈ A with du(a) invertible. Then u restricts to a homeomorphism from an open neighbourhood U of a onto an open neighbourhood V of u(a), and the inverse map is analytic.

Remark on global injectivity.
- For K = R and A an open interval, u' ≠ 0 forces u to be monotone (Darboux), so u is a homeomorphism of all of A onto u(A).
- For K = C this fails. Take u(x) = x^n on the disc |x−1| < 1/2. Then u' ≠ 0 there, but for n large the disc contains n-th roots of unity other than 1, so u is not injective.

Editorial note: the functional-dependence theorem (holomorphic functions with identically vanishing Jacobian) 'should also be done here'.

§3, Theorem 2 (Cauchy existence and uniqueness, analytic in parameters). Over a complete valued field K of characteristic 0, let f_i(x; y; z) be analytic near (a; b; c). Then there are neighbourhoods U, V, W and a unique system of analytic u_i(x; z) on U×W with values in V. The page ends before stating the defining conditions, which are presumably ∂u_i/∂x = f_i(x; u; z) with u_i(a; z) = b_i.

The purpose of the page is foundational: building the local theory of analytic manifolds over arbitrary complete valued fields, archimedean or not.
errors: No mathematical errors. The x^n example is correct: |e^{2πi/n} − 1| = 2 sin(π/n) < 1/2 once n ≥ 13.

The characteristic-0 hypothesis is needed for the ODE theorem, since integrating power series divides by n. It is not needed for the inverse function theorem, which the page does not restrict, so this is consistent.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Bourbaki-type foundational draft on analytic functions over valued fields, unrelated to the motivic notes around it. The only point of mild archival interest is the fact that this typescript sits in the motives dossier.
transcription_corrections: The heading 'THEOREME 2' is partly faint and appears as 'THEOREME' in the image; the transcription is otherwise accurate.
The index range reads (1 ≤ i ≤ p); the first character is faint.
The margin pencil number '46' is the archive page number, not part of the text.
The page breaks off at 'aux conditions'; the ODE conditions themselves are on the following typescript page, which is not the 'next page' given here.
